title: Sidebar
description: The shell's navigation in two layouts. Trimmed port of the shadcn sidebar, inset variant only, icon collapse only, for the left column; below 40rem of the wrapper's width the same nav items move to a bottom Dock (dock.tsx, same family). Compound component: the consumer arranges named parts as JSX; each part owns its own chrome. Nav items render router links via asChild; active styling keys off aria-current="page".

anatomy.description: Owns open/collapsed state (controlled or uncontrolled) and exposes it through useSidebar. Sets the width custom properties on the wrapper. Measures the wrapper's width into a store and publishes layout: "sidebar" | "dock" (below SIDEBAR_DOCK_BELOW, 640px) through useSidebar, mirrored as data-layout on the wrapper; in dock layout state always reads expanded, so the strip shows the full switcher.
The navigation column; data-state="expanded|collapsed" drives the collapse animation.
Mini discrete Button that toggles the sidebar; the label is visually hidden with the global sr-only class.

The <main> scroll container beside the sidebar (the document never scrolls). Measures its own width with a ResizeObserver into an external store; useSidebarInset(narrowBelow = SIDEBAR_INSET_NARROW_WIDTH, 704px) subscribes with a selector and returns a boolean that re-renders the caller only when it flips, useSidebarInsetWidth() returns the raw number; data-narrow mirrors the house-threshold boolean. Content inside adapts to this signal, never to the viewport. Also publishes its scroll direction ("up" | "down", mirrored as data-scroll on the wrapper) for the dock: "down" after a 12px turn downward and only while the content exceeds the inset by more than 72px, "up" after a 12px turn upward or within 8px of the top.

Zero-height sticky anchor at the top of the inset that floats the SidebarTrigger in the inset's reserved left gutter (--sidebar-inset-gutter, 3rem), so the toggle stays present while the inset scrolls and shares a row with sticky toolbars and table headers without any offset. Hidden by CSS in dock layout, where the gutter resolves to 0.

Dock layout only: the band of ground above the inset that holds the TenantSwitcher once there is no sidebar header. The switcher keeps its own surface and its inline disclosure, which pushes the inset down (B′, chosen 2026-09-23 at /lab/dock). One tight row: the switcher compacts itself here by CSS on the wrapper's data-layout (smaller tile, name and plan inline, chevron always visible).

Vertical regions of the column: the header holds the TenantSwitcher, the content the tenant's groups and scrolls, the footer the session's exit (a Log out row in its own SidebarMenu, added 2026-09-28) pinned at the foot.
A labelled cluster of menu items.

The nav list. SidebarMenu draws a sliding indicator shaped as an inset-connector tab under the active item (aria-current="page" or data-active) or under an open disclosure row (aria-expanded="true"); SidebarMenuButton slots a router link with asChild or renders a react-aria Button.

Attention indicator: a heartwood-400 dot ringed in the rail's green, floating just after the row's label (rendered inside the button before the label span, reordered by CSS so the label stays the last child that doubles as the rail tooltip); on the icon's corner in the collapsed rail; no ring on the active row, where it sits on the bark-50 pill. Purely visual and aria-hidden — the words for screen readers live inside the label as sr-only text. Never a pointer target.

Dock layout only: the <nav> at the foot of the wrapper (aria-label "Primary" by default), padded by the phone's bottom safe area. Owns the open state of More; data-expanded while the panel is open, when it wears the switcher's glass blob. Scrolls away: under [data-scroll="down"] it slides beneath the screen's edge and hands the inset its 3.5rem, keeping the safe-area band; never while open or while a cell has focus.
The <ul> of cells. A plain list: the active cell (aria-current="page" or data-active) wears the needle pill by CSS, nothing measures.

One cell: icon over an --text-xs label (the accessible name), a SidebarMenuBadge on the glyph's corner when the item is badged. asChild slots a router link; otherwise a react-aria Button. Needle-950 at rest, bloom outline on focus; active, the icon alone sits on a needle-200 pill and the label stays on the ground (theming §4.7, selection in needle). The active cell takes no pointer.

The fifth cell, present whenever there is anything the row does not show: a disclosure trigger (aria-expanded, aria-controls) for DockPanel. Takes a badge when a badged item is hidden behind it, and the sr-only words inside its label.

What More discloses: a grid-rows 0fr to 1fr panel (the switcher's mechanism) that grows the dock upward and pushes the inset up, inert while closed. Filled with the sidebar's own menu parts (SidebarGroup, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton); the menu's indicator is hidden inside it. Escape closes it and returns focus to More; choosing a row closes it.

usage: Wrap the layout in SidebarProvider; read layout from useSidebar() and render Sidebar, or SidebarStrip and Dock, beside one SidebarInset, never both navigations. The inset is the same element in both layouts, so scroll position, the width store and data-narrow survive the swap; every difference in its chrome is CSS against the wrapper's data-layout.
Scrolling happens inside SidebarInset, not the document: size sticky offsets against the inset's top edge, and never rely on window.scrollY.

Read useSidebarInset(threshold) to adapt a component to the space it actually has (the leads table becomes cards, the filter bar folds into a drawer). The inset publishes the fact (its width); each consumer owns the policy (its threshold) as a named constant beside its content, defaulting to the house value so the common case switches together. Outside an inset the hook reports wide.

Never debounce the inset signal: ResizeObserver already coalesces to one notification per frame and the selector re-renders a consumer only when its boolean flips, so a delay would only leave content in the wrong layout mid-resize.
Sticky content inside the inset pins to top: 0; the floating trigger lives in the inset's left gutter, so nothing needs to offset for it.

Mark the active item with the router's aria-current="page" (or data-active); the indicator observes both and needs no router coupling. The active item takes no pointer: it is the current page. A row that discloses a panel sets aria-expanded and aria-controls instead (component-architecture §5.3): open, it reads like the active item and takes the indicator, but stays pressable so the same press closes it.
Collapsed-rail labels need no tooltip component: the row's own label is repositioned and revealed on hover/focus by CSS, so the accessible name stays on the button.
Deliberately not ported: floating/right variants, offcanvas mode, the mobile sheet (narrow shells switch to the Dock instead), rail/input/separator, submenus, cookie persistence, keyboard shortcut.
Badges carry attention only: heartwood is the identity's one red, so a badge means something needs acting on (leads pending analysis), not decoration. Render nothing when the count is 0.

Actions on the session (Log out) go in SidebarFooter as a SidebarMenu row rendered as a react-aria Button (no asChild), so they wear the nav's face, collapse to their icon with the rail and keep the label as the collapsed tooltip. The shell owns where a log-out lands; the row only reports the press. Rows in the rail are the one place an icon is required (component-architecture §3.10): collapsed, the icon is all that shows. Development tooling follows the same pattern: the shell's query and router devtools are footer rows above Log out that disclose (aria-expanded, aria-controls; never isActive, which would take the pointer away) a dock stuck to the foot of the inset, in place of the libraries' floating corner buttons.

Tag nav items for the dock with NavItem.surfaces (["sidebar"] by default; "dock" or both). The dock shows tagged items in tree order, four at most; the shell puts everything else, then Log out, behind More, so a sidebar-only item stays reachable and no tenant loses its exit. A badge hidden behind More moves to More. The rule is a pure function of the tree (dockItems in src/lib/api.ts) and lives in the shell route, not in the component.
The dock is the second place an icon is required (component-architecture §3.10): a cell is its icon over a word.

Width alone picks the layout, at SIDEBAR_DOCK_BELOW measured on the wrapper: a narrow desktop window gets the dock, tablet portrait keeps the sidebar. Never debounce the signal, for the same reason as the inset's.

Swapping layouts while focus is inside the navigation hands focus to the active item of the new navigation (or its first item); the shell route owns that handoff, the parts only record that they held focus.
The dock hides on scroll by CSS against the wrapper's data-scroll; nothing in the shell route wires it. A page that barely overflows keeps its dock, so do not pad a short page to force the behaviour.
